name: GoGo Board 7 version 3.2.5
body:
## This firmware powers the `GoGo Board 7`, unlocking advanced hardware capabilities that inspire children to explore computational thinking through creativity and play.

### What's new in this version

#### Stability & Fixes
- Fixed Logo programs losing their variables. Any program using a background block, a message subscription, or a "when" condition silently reset variables that had already been set back to zero.
- Fixed motors not responding when the run duration came from a variable, which stopped the motor almost immediately instead of running for the set time.
- Fixed repeat blocks not running when the repeat count came from a variable.
- Fixed wait blocks not pausing when the delay came from a variable.
- Fixed text variables being stored as a number, which caused recorded sequences to play back as nothing.

### Minimum hardware requirement
GoGo Board version 7 or above

### How to upgrade to this version
- Auto update. When existing firmware is version 2.5.0 or above, update can take place within the [code.gogoboard.org](https://code.gogoboard.org) environment.
- Manual update. Visit [install-firmware.gogoboard.org](https://install-firmware.gogoboard.org/) and follow the instructions.
  > [Firmware update manual](https://github.com/arnans/gogodoc/blob/main/firmware-update/firmware-update-guide.md)

### Known issues
- Microphone not working. (in development)
- IR transmitter not working. (in development)

---

## Bundled co-MCU firmware

### vernier v2.1.0

# vernier-firmware v2.1.0

Released 2026-05-23. Reported in T_HELLO as `firmware_id=vernier,
version_major=2, version_minor=1, version_patch=0`. Minor bump —
**fully wire-compatible with v2.0.0 hosts**; the new keys and
command are additive. `VERNIER_PROTOCOL_VERSION` stays at 2.

## Highlights

- **Non-blocking BLE connect** — `dev.connect()` runs on a new
  `bleWorker` FreeRTOS task instead of stalling the host-protocol
  UART task for ~5–7 s during the BLE scan + GATT handshake. Host
  commands keep flowing while a slot pairs.
- **Early-ACK semantics** — `C_CONNECT` ACKs `ok=true msg="queued"`
  within milliseconds of arrival. Outcome (success or failure)
  reaches the host via the auto-pushed `T_DEV_LIST` (Q3 piggyback).
  No second ACK on completion — single ACK per command preserved.
- **`C_CANCEL_CONNECT` (wire value 6)** — abort a still-queued
  C_CONNECT before bleWorker picks it up. Implemented as an atomic
  CAS REQUESTED → IDLE; loses cleanly if the worker already started
  the handshake (NACK `msg="not pending"`).
- **`T_DEV_LIST.slots[].state:u8`** — optional per-entry field
  carrying the slot's `ConnState` numeric value (0=IDLE,
  1=REQUESTED, 2=CONNECTING, 3=READY). Lets the host render a
  CONNECTING spinner without inferring state from the absence of
  T_DEVINFO. Pre-2.1.0 hosts ignore the key.

## Wire / behaviour changes (host MUST handle)

- **Single ACK per `C_CONNECT`.** The ACK arrives early (`msg=
  "queued"`) instead of after the BLE handshake settles. Hosts
  that gate on the ACK to render "connected" state must instead
  watch for `connected:true` or `state:3` (READY) in the next
  auto-pushed T_DEV_LIST.
- **CONNECTING is now a real wire-visible state.** Hosts can render
  a spinner while `state == 2` instead of after the request +
  before T_DEVINFO arrives.
- **`C_CONNECT` on a slot in REQUESTED / CONNECTING / READY
  returns NACK `"slot busy"`** instead of stalling. Pre-2.1.0
  hosts wouldn't have seen this because the connect was blocking;
  add a guard if the host fires C_CONNECT speculatively.
- **`C_CANCEL_CONNECT` is best-effort once the worker has CAS'd into
  CONNECTING.** NimBLE has no in-flight scan cancel — cancel during
  CONNECTING NACKs `"not pending"`. Host UI should gate the cancel
  button on `state == REQUESTED` (or just `connected == false`).

## Fixes

- C_CONNECT no longer leaves the UART task parked inside NimBLE for
  ~7 s. (The centerpiece of this release.)
- T_FIELDS now always lands before the first T_SENS_VALUES for a
  newly-ready slot. The bleWorker → publishConnectResult ordering
  was inverted in an earlier draft (G007 commit `6b554a4`); the
  fix in `da5e19c` hoists the terminal `setState(READY)` to the
  tail of publishConnectResult, after every uart.send* + a
  compiler reordering barrier.
- `cmdSetPeriod` NACKs sub-`VERNIER_MIN_PERIOD_MS` (10 ms) requests
  with `msg="period below min"` instead of forwarding them to
  GoGoVernier (which would spin start/stop trying to honor the
  unhonorable period).
- `FramedMsgPackReceiver` logs `deserializeMsgPack` failures at
  `log_w` so wire corruption is observable in the field.
- `UartAdapter::send()` had a stale-`_doc` early-return that could
  leak keys into the next frame on oversize payload — fixed in
  v2.0.0's tail and carried forward.

### Multi-device reconnect (found by the v2.1.0 hardware smoke)

These three were latent since v2.0.0 — the multi-device path was
never hardware-smoked until this release. All only bite when more
than one saved sensor reconnects, which is why they survived 2.0.0.

- **Only the first slot reconnected** after a power-cycle with 3
  saved sensors. The host sends one `C_SET_PERIOD` per slot at boot,
  each re-arming auto-connect, so `autoConnectDevice` ran several
  times; `enqueueConnect` did an unconditional `setState(REQUESTED)`
  + rollback-to-IDLE on the (now-full) queue, corrupting slots that
  already had valid queued requests. Fixed by claiming the slot with
  a CAS `IDLE→REQUESTED` — duplicate enqueues are now clean no-ops.
- **Earlier slots stuck "connecting" ~30 s** while only the last
  slot showed values. `T_HELLO` was emitted on every connect, and
  the host resets its whole connection state on `T_HELLO`, so each
  slot's connect wiped the previously-connected slots' display.
  `T_HELLO`+`T_STATUS` are now a once-per-session boot handshake
  (first host command), not per-connect.
- **Disconnect/forget while a slot is mid-handshake** could leave it
  shown-connected-but-gone, or stuck READY-never-streaming — the
  worker's READY publish raced `disconnect()`'s IDLE store with no
  ordering. `publishConnectResult` now CASes `CONNECTING→READY` and
  abandons (tears the link back down) if a disconnect won the race.

## Internal

- New `bleWorker` FreeRTOS task at the same priority as
  uartHandler / vernierHandler. Single producer of `dev.connect()`
  / `dev.disconnect()` from G007 onward — drops the "GDXLib
  internal serialization" assumption that the 2.0.0 review flagged.
- Per-slot connection lifecycle state machine — `ConnState` enum
  (IDLE / REQUESTED / CONNECTING / READY) backed by
  `std::atomic<ConnState>` on `VernierAdapter`. Producers use
  `tryAcquireConnecting()` (CAS REQUESTED → CONNECTING) and
  `tryCancelConnect()` (CAS REQUESTED → IDLE) to make the
  bleWorker-vs-cancel race deterministic.
- H6 per-slot recursive status mutex on VernierAdapter. Closes the
  torn-read race where vernierHandler's 10 s status refresh could
  race a bleWorker `getDeviceInfo` mid-handshake. Recursive so
  callers can wrap `(getDeviceInfo + multi-field read)` under one
  `lockStatus()` without deadlocking on the nested take inside
  getDeviceInfo.
- H1 `static_assert(VERNIER_MAX_SLOTS <= CONFIG_BT_NIMBLE_MAX_CONNECTIONS)`
  in `vernier-adapter.cpp` so a future slot bump can't silently
  overflow NimBLE.
- H2 `VernierAdapter::_period_ms` and `_push_dropped` promoted from
  volatile to `std::atomic<>` with `memory_order_relaxed`. Drops
  the manual load/store pattern that side-stepped C++20's
  `-Wdeprecated-volatile`.
- `connectAndReport` retired — replaced by `enqueueConnect`
  (cmdConnect / button / autoConnect producer side) +
  `bleWorkerEntry` + `publishConnectResult` (worker resolution
  side).
- `HANDLER_TASK_PRIO` and `TASK_STACK_BLE_HEAVY` hoisted to
  `include/main.h` so the uartHandler + bleWorker stack sizes
  share one source of truth.
- `isReady()` switched to `state() == ConnState::READY` (was
  routing through `_gv.isReady()`). The state publish runs AFTER
  the side-effect burst in `publishConnectResult`, with a
  compiler barrier between the last `uart.send*` and the
  state-store, so vernierHandler can't observe READY before
  T_FIELDS has shipped.
- `disconnect()` flips state to IDLE so emitDevList / vernierHandler
  see the slot as free immediately instead of waiting for the
  next connect attempt to overwrite the state.
- `isSlotOccupied` rewritten as `state() != IDLE` so a slot
  mid-REQUESTED/CONNECTING isn't falsely returned by
  `firstFreeSlot()`.
- Boot hand-off globals (`startAutoConnect`, `foundSavedDevice`,
  `slotHasSavedDevice[]`) promoted from `volatile` + `__asm__`
  barrier to `std::atomic` with release/acquire on the two gate
  flags (relaxed on the data array). Expresses the publish ordering
  portably instead of leaning on the single-core context-switch
  barrier.
- Two rounds of pre-tag deslop: removed defensive code for
  can't-happen scenarios (worker slot-range recheck, bleWorkerStart
  partial-failure recovery, ctor null-guards on process-lifetime
  mutex/queue) and deleted the unreachable `ConnState::FAILED` enum
  value (re-addable as value 4 at the end of the enum if a future
  host-UX needs a distinct failure signal). Net code shrink.

### tasmota gogo-4451f8f

# tasmota-build gogo-4451f8f

Built 2026-03-18 against the GoGo-specific Tasmota fork (tag
`gogo-4451f8f`). This is the bootstrap entry — captures the binary
that was sitting in `tasmota-build/build_output/firmware/` when the
`co-mcu-firmware/` directory was first populated.

## What this firmware is

Tasmota build customised for the GoGo Board 7 ESP32-C3 co-MCU
slot. Lets the host treat any ESP32-C3 running this binary as a
Tasmota smart-device controller (relays, sensors, MQTT) reachable
through the host's network stack.

## How it differs from upstream Tasmota

- **Variant:** ESP32-C3 (`tasmota32c3`) — see `boards/` and
  `platformio_tasmota32.ini` in the tasmota-build repo for the GoGo
  build flags.
- **Naming:** factory image is named `gogo-co-firmware-tasmota32c3.factory.bin`
  to match the gogo-firmware co-MCU naming convention.

## Upstream release notes

This bootstrap entry doesn't summarise upstream Tasmota changes —
the changeset since the previous gogo-* tag is too large to capture
manually. Future releases will use the `release-comcu` skill to diff
`gogo-<prev>..HEAD` and group by conventional-commit type.

For upstream Tasmota changes since v15.x, see
<https://github.com/arendst/Tasmota/blob/master/RELEASENOTES.md>.

## How to refresh this entry

In `tasmota-build/`:

```
# After a new GoGo-specific build:
git tag gogo-<short-sha>
/release-comcu      # bundles into ../gogo-firmware/co-mcu-firmware/
```
